subject: Re: GCP Private Offer — invoice waterfall & smoothing proposal
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lee <procurement@bluebirdhealth.com>, finance@bluebirdhealth.com
Cc: Rena Patel <gcp-partner@google.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: GCP Private Offer — invoice waterfall & smoothing proposal

Hi Anna — great to be progressing here. Attaching a first-pass invoice schedule and a suggested waterfall for drawdowns against the private offer. Two quick notes: 1) GCP private offers require monthly drawdown events tied to invoice dates in most regions; 2) we can set a smoothing policy that amortizes committed usage across months to avoid large single-month invoices (helps internal finance).

Can you confirm Bluebird's preferred billing cadence (monthly vs. quarterly) and whether you need PO-level line items or a single subscription line? Rena, cc'd, can you confirm if the private offer link needs any partner-side tweaks for the waterfall logic?

Next steps: if Bluebird confirms cadence today we can finalize the private offer in GCP and push a DocuSign with the invoice schedule by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee | Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0123

Attachments (3): Bluebird_PO_Draft_20260701.pdf (pdf), Redwood_GCP_Private_Offer_Terms.xlsx (xlsx), Invoice_Schedule_Proposal.csv (csv)

From: Anna Lee <procurement@bluebirdhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@bluebirdhealth.com
Date: 2026-07-02T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GCP Private Offer — invoice waterfall & smoothing proposal

Hi Soojin — thanks for the materials. A few clarifying items from our side: 1) Bluebird prefers monthly invoices with net-30 payment terms; 2) we need line-item detail for committed units on the PO for internal cost centers (separate lines for inference tokens and embeddings); 3) can you confirm whether smoothing will still allow us to spike usage for clinical pilot months without breaching covenant?

Finance (cc) — any legal/PO-format requirements we should flag? We can provide a PO template if helpful.

Anna
Anna Lee | Sr. Procurement Manager
Bluebird Health
procurement@bluebirdhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Anna Lee <procurement@bluebirdhealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-03T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: GCP Private Offer — invoice waterfall & smoothing proposal

Forwarding Anna's asks — quick notes from Legal/Finance POV: 
- We can emit line-item level POs. Redwood's standard is to map committed units to SKU lines (tokens, embeddings).
- Smoothing: we can implement a monthly amortization policy on the backend so invoices show equalized committed spend, but true usage overage will still be billed as overage at the month it occurs. We can add an "overage guard" clause to allow for 20% monthly spikes without immediate penalty (trial/pilot protection).

Marissa — confirm whether accounting can accept a monthly amortized invoice that reconciles actual usage as a separate overage line on the following invoice. Also confirm whether we can set a soft cap notification at 80% commit.

Ben
Ben Carter | Head of Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Lee <procurement@bluebirdhealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-04T10:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GCP Private Offer — invoice waterfall & smoothing proposal

Ben / Soojin — finance confirms we can produce an amortized monthly invoice for the committed amount and then show usage reconciliation as a separate line item the following month. Requirements/constraints: 
- PO must include SKU-level commit quantities and the committed term (12 months).
- We will auto-generate monthly invoices for the amortized committed spend. Any usage over the commit in a month will appear as "usage overage" on next invoice with clear unit pricing.
- For pilot protection, we can add a one-time 20% buffer where the first two months of overage under 20% are waived; after that, standard overage rates apply. This needs to be in the private offer terms and reflected in the GCP partner config.

I attached a sample invoice CSV (Invoice_Schedule_Proposal.csv) to show layout. Ben, can Legal add the 20% buffer language into the private offer?

Marissa Cole | Finance, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lee <procurement@bluebirdhealth.com>, finance@bluebirdhealth.com
Cc: Rena Patel <gcp-partner@google.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-07T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GCP Private Offer — invoice waterfall & smoothing proposal

Anna — great, thanks for confirming cadence. Per finance and sales ops: we'll publish the private offer with: 
- Monthly amortized committed invoices (12-month term, SKU-level lines)
- Usage overage reconciliation on the following invoice with unit-level pricing
- Pilot protection: first two months of overage up to 20% waived (explicit clause included)

Next steps for Bluebird: 1) please confirm PO template (we attached Bluebird_PO_Draft_20260701.pdf as a starting point), 2) confirm billing contact and mailing address for invoicing, 3) once confirmed we will create the private offer in the GCP console and send the DocuSign link (include the invoice schedule) for signatures.

Rena — any action on the Google side to ensure the private offer metadata includes the amortization/display rules and the 20% pilot flag?

Thanks all — happy to hop on a 20-min call if anyone wants to walk through the invoice preview.

Best,
Soojin
Attachments (1): Bluebird_PO_Draft_20260701.pdf (pdf)
